user.title: Add IG Doorbell
user.description: Enter the doorbell's IP address on your local network (skip this if it already showed up as a discovered device). Home Assistant talks to the doorbell only over the local network, never through the internet.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Doorbell found on the network
zeroconf_confirm.description: Found {name} via mDNS. Continue to pair it.

pair.title: Pair with {name}
pair.description: Enter the administrator email and password you already created on the doorbell itself (app or web dashboard). Used once to obtain an access credential - never stored.

entities.title: Entities the doorbell can act on
entities.description: Pick the entities you want to be able to trigger from the doorbell - to unlock the door, or from a step in one of its sequences. Only these will be offered in the apps. Up to {max}.

address.title: Doorbell address
address.description: The doorbell's IP address on your local network. Change it if the doorbell moved (new IP or VLAN). Home Assistant only reaches the doorbell at this address.

repair.title: Re-pair
repair.description: Use this if the access credential was revoked. Enter the doorbell's administrator email/password again.

https.title: Secure local connection (HTTPS)
https.description:
Serves this Home Assistant over HTTPS on your home network, on a port of its own, so browsers let the doorbell card use the microphone (two-way audio). Off by default. Home Assistant's own port and settings are not touched.

**This is not remote access.** It does not replace Home Assistant Cloud or your own domain with a reverse proxy.

It gives two addresses:
- **Public name** – nothing to install on your devices. A publicly trusted certificate for a name like `<id>.ha.doorbell.islautopia.com`. Needs an IG Doorbell paired here as administrator and registered with the Islautopia cloud: the doorbell vouches for this Home Assistant. Only for this is the cloud contacted, and it never receives the certificate's private key. Needs internet to look up the name.
- **Local address** (IP or homeassistant.local) – works without internet and without a doorbell. The certificate comes from this integration's own local certificate authority: install its root certificate once on each device.

Set up your devices: [install page]({install_url}) · [How it works]({docs_url})

data_description.enabled: Opens the HTTPS port and keeps its certificates up to date.
data_description.port: Default 8443. It must be free on the Home Assistant machine.

notifications.title: Ring notifications
notifications.description: Home Assistant rings the phones and wall panels you pick here when someone presses the bell, with the visitor's picture, and clears them everywhere as soon as the call is answered. Nothing to write: no automation needed. Leave both lists empty to turn this off (if you already have your own automation for the bell, turn one of the two off or every ring will arrive twice). Opening the call page or the picture from outside the house needs remote access to Home Assistant; talking needs a secure page (HTTPS).

data.panel_return_path: Panel: page to return to after the call
data.announce_voice: Also say which doorbell is ringing

data_description.notify_phones: Companion-app phones. They get a notification with the picture; tapping it opens the call page.
data_description.notify_panels: Companion-app tablets on the wall. Android: the screen wakes and shows the call page (the companion app needs the "Display over other apps" permission, or it silently shows a plain notification instead). iPad: a notification; leave the call page open in Guided Access for a real panel.
data_description.notify_critical: iPhone: critical alert (allow Critical Alerts for the Home Assistant app). Android: alarm stream.
data_description.notify_open_door: Adds an "Open door" button to the notification, valid only during the ring. iPhone asks for Face ID first. On Android it is not yet known whether the phone must be unlocked - leave it off if that matters.
data_description.panel_return_path: For example /lovelace/0. Empty: the Home Assistant app's home page.
data_description.announce_players: They play a doorbell chime when someone rings: Alexa (Echo) its own doorbell chime, every other speaker the IG Doorbell chime. If you already announce the bell on these speakers with an automation, you don't need this - or they will announce twice.
data_description.announce_voice: Alexa: an announcement; other speakers: needs a text-to-speech engine in Home Assistant.

play_sequence.name: Play sequence
play_sequence.description: Run one of the doorbell's sequences (a quick reply that can speak, turn on a light or extend the recording).

seq_id.name: Sequence id
seq_id.description: Id of the sequence on the doorbell.

play_audio.name: Play quick reply
play_audio.description: Play the audio stored in a quick-reply slot through the doorbell's speaker.

https_port_in_use.title: Secure local connection: port {port} is taken
https_port_in_use.description: Another program already uses port {port}, so the secure local connection (HTTPS) could not start. Choose another port in Settings › Devices & services › Islautopia Garage Doorbell › Configure › Secure local connection (HTTPS). Nothing else is affected.

https_unsupported.title: Secure local connection not supported
https_unsupported.description: This version of Home Assistant does not let the integration serve HTTPS the way it needs. The secure local connection is off; everything else works. Update Home Assistant or the integration.

https_public_name_admin_required.title: Public name unavailable: guest pairing
https_public_name_admin_required.description: The doorbell only vouches for a Home Assistant paired as administrator, and this one is paired as a guest (user). The secure local address works as usual: install its root certificate on your devices from the install page. To get the public name, re-pair with an administrator account (Configure › Re-pair).

https_public_name_not_registered.title: Public name unavailable: doorbell not registered
https_public_name_not_registered.description: The doorbell is not registered with the Islautopia cloud, so it cannot vouch for this Home Assistant. The secure local address works as usual: install its root certificate on your devices from the install page.

https_public_name_taken.title: The doorbell's public name belongs to another Home Assistant

confirm.title: Move the public name here?
confirm.description:
Each doorbell has one public name for Home Assistant, and {hostname} is currently used by another Home Assistant. If this one should have it (for example after reinstalling), move it here. The other one keeps working until its certificate expires and then only has its local address.

The public name will point to this Home Assistant and its certificate will be issued for it. The other Home Assistant will not be able to renew its certificate.

https_public_name_failed.title: Public name unavailable
https_public_name_failed.description: The public name for Home Assistant could not be obtained ({code}). The secure local address is not affected. The integration's documentation explains each code.
